Chapter 1
Introduction
1.1
Background
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the way people search, analyze, and inter-
act with information. Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) such as LLaMA, GPT,
and Mistral can understand natural language queries and generate human-like responses.
However, these models often rely on their pre-trained knowledge and may produce inac-
curate or fabricated information, commonly known as hallucinations.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as an effective solution to this
limitation by combining information retrieval with language generation. Instead of an-
swering solely from model memory, a RAG system first retrieves relevant information
from user-provided documents and then generates responses based only on that retrieved
context. This significantly improves answer accuracy, reliability, and transparency.
The Intelligent Research Assistant developed during this internship is based on the
RAG architecture. The application enables users to upload research documents, organize
them into personal workspaces, perform semantic document search, and obtain grounded
responses with citations generated by a local Large Language Model.
1.2
Project Overview
The Intelligent Research Assistant is a web-based application designed to provide secure
document management and intelligent question answering over user-uploaded documents.
The application is implemented using FastAPI as the backend framework together
with SQLAlchemy, SQLite, MongoDB, JWT authentication, Sentence Transformers,
FAISS Vector Database, and Ollama running the LLaMA 3 model locally.
The system follows a complete Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline consisting
